hints.title: Extreme Value Allocation
hints.text: Maintain the minimum available integer and the maximum available integer from the pool [0, n].

hints.title: Greedy Low-High Tracking
hints.text: Whenever an I is encountered, greedily assign the smallest available number so the next number is guaranteed to be larger.

hints.title: Single-Pass Permutation Construction
hints.text: Initialize low = 0 and high = n. For each char in s: if c == "I", append low and increment low; else append high and decrement high. Finally append low (which equals high) to complete the n+1 length permutation.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating permutations of 0 to n has factorial complexity O((N+1)!), which is impossible for N up to 10000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy selection of extreme values produces a valid arrangement in a single linear scan with O(N) output space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should quickly deduce that selecting the minimum for I and maximum for D leaves all remaining elements valid for subsequent choices.
complexity.notes: Any valid permutation is accepted; greedy extreme placement is the canonical simplest approach.
